Love this app. I’ve been using Picture Mushroom for quite a while, and it’s become one of my favorite apps. I love exploring the outdoors and photographing wild mushrooms, and this app makes the entire process both educational and fun. The identification feature is fast, easy to use, and has helped me learn about countless species I would have otherwise never recognized.

What I appreciate most is how it encourages curiosity. Instead of just walking past mushrooms, I’m constantly stopping to take photos and learn something new. The app’s interface is user-friendly, and the information provided is detailed enough to keep both beginners and experienced mushroom enthusiasts engaged.

Of course, mushroom identification can be incredibly complex, and no app can be perfect. My only wish is that there were a way to achieve 100% certainty on every identification. Some species are simply too similar to distinguish from a photo alone. That said, Picture Mushroom does an impressive job and has greatly enhanced my mushroom-hunting experiences.

Overall, it’s a fantastic app that I use regularly and would highly recommend to anyone interested in mushrooms, nature, or learning more about the world around them.

I took two hours. It took 20 seconds.. I love mushrooms as much as steak. Maybe more, since mushrooms are free and come in a variety of favors and textures, where steak is only measured by tenderness and how you cook it. I recently ran across a bloom of funnel shaped mushrooms in a park in southern Minnesota, and I collected every one I could see in the hopes that I might have discovered a feast.

When I got home, I put them all in the fridge, since I knew identifying a new species takes hours, and I was tired. The only identification I did was remember where I'd found them, and lay out a spoor print.

 (For aspiring mushroom lovers, a spoor print is where you cut off the stem and put the cap on a piece of paper, so you can see what color the spoors are.
It usually only takes a half hour or so. It's not always important, but I have lost count of the times I have collected a bunch of parasol mushrooms, spoor print every color but blue or green, and false parasol with a blue or green spoor print. FYI parasols are considered among the most delicious, while the false parasol also has the common name "the vomiter" for good reason. People have died of dehydration from not taking a spoor print, when they look exactly the same.) 

The next morning, I spent two or three hours identifying this mushroom. I thought I had it dead to rights identified as Lactarius Psammicola, but southern Minnesota is a bit outside its recorded range. So I looked at reviews from mycologists, and picked an app that had solid professionals who recommended it.

It took the app 20 seconds to tell me Lactarius Psammicola, I verified with established mycologists that I had Lactarius psammicola. 

Funny enough, I don't taste bitter very well. The "acrid taste" in the description literally means unpleasant and distinctive. Lactarius psammicola just uses tannic acid it gets from oak tree symbiosis as defense, which means it has a bitter aftertaste that I can't taste.

It turns out that the Lactarius Psammicola was a delicious feast, just only for me, not my wife or kids.
